text: Reproduce it: `shipnotify-log 'test message'` then check `/var/log/shipnotify/shipnotify.log`. Nothing. rsyslog isn't erroring anywhere, and there's no obviously suspicious debug rule sitting in `/etc/rsyslog.d/25-shipnotify.conf` routing anything to `/dev/null` -- that rule looks completely correct.
The rule is correct for the facility it names (`local3.*`) -- so check whether shipnotify is actually sending on that facility at all. Look at how it logs: `cat /usr/local/bin/shipnotify-log`.

It's tagged `-p mail.info`, not `local3`. That's a real, legitimate syslog facility -- and rsyslog's own stock, unmodified default config already has a rule for it: `grep mail /etc/rsyslog.conf` shows `mail.*  -/var/log/mail.log`, installed by the rsyslog package itself, long before shipnotify existed. Check `/var/log/mail.log` -- that's exactly where the messages have been going.

Fix the facility shipnotify actually logs on to match the dedicated rule that was written for it: `sudo sed -i 's/-p mail.info/-p local3.info/' /usr/local/bin/shipnotify-log`. No rsyslog restart needed -- the routing rule was always correct, only the app's own facility tag was wrong. Verify: `shipnotify-log 'confirm'` then `tail /var/log/shipnotify/shipnotify.log`.
